svg.title: CloudMart identity and access diagram
svg.desc: How CloudMart authenticates and authorises. Microsoft Entra ID issues user tokens through the SPA and API app registrations (scope access_as_user, app role CloudMart.Admin), service tokens for the Payments and Shipping app roles, and federated tokens for AKS workload identity and the pipeline's service connection. A matrix lists every Azure RBAC role, Cosmos DB data-plane role, SQL database user and Entra app role held by each identity. No keys or connection-string secrets are used.
svg.text: Who signs in, how services get tokens, and every role each identity holds. No keys or connection-string secrets anywhere: every arrow is an Entra ID token.
¹ ² ³ ⁴ = not Azure RBAC (see footnotes)
Microsoft Entra ID · your tenant: three ways CloudMart gets a token
CloudMart Payments and CloudMart Shipping (two app registrations)

text.tspan: App roles Payments.Process and Shipments.Manage, allowedMemberTypes: Application, assigned to both
identities through Microsoft Graph. Each caller asks for api://<app>/.default with client credentials;
the token carries roles and no scp, because no user is involved.
identity, no secret in the pod

svg.text: ¹ Phase 16 moves the payment-gateway key: only the Payments identity can read it, and the API and Functions lose access.
² Cosmos DB data-plane RBAC (sqlRoleAssignments: Built-in Data Contributor). It is not Azure RBAC, so the IAM blade doesn't show it.

³ Contained database users (CREATE USER ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER) from deploy/sql/grant-managed-identities.sql, not Azure RBAC. ddladmin only because the apps create their schema; production runs migrations from the pipeline.
⁴ Entra app roles (application permissions) on the services' app registrations, assigned through Microsoft Graph, not Azure RBAC. The phase 11 Event Hubs secondary gets the same roles as the primary.
Control plane is not data plane

text.tspan: Owner and Contributor manage resources, but read
no blobs, secrets or messages: that takes a data role.
Shared keys off on Storage; local auth off on Service
Bus and Event Hubs; Cosmos DB keys off; SQL Entra-only.
Sender or receiver, never both; a secret readable by one
service; a database per service; app roles per API.
